evals.prompt: Here's transactions.csv from our payment gateway (300 rows). I want it queryable in plain English on this Mac, through our neuralOS/needle stack — and I want a strict Pydantic model of what's in it.
evals.expected_output: Runs the 4-phase workflow: profile_data.py on the CSV, reads the profile, gen_pydantic.py -> models.py (verified by instantiating), gen_needle_instance.py -> instance dir, then actually asks the generated instance a question and runs verify.py coverage.

evals.prompt: We have an app.log with thousands of lines in mixed formats (timestamps, levels, services, IPs). Build a needle instance that can parse and count them — errors per level, tail parsing, substring search. Offline only.
evals.expected_output: Profiler synthesizes line templates with capture regexes; generated models include per-template classes + parse_line; generated menu has parse_tail/count_by_level/search_log; verification shows high parse coverage and a correct level count.

evals.prompt: Profile the efraud MySQL database (localhost:3306, admin/admin) and give me a needle instance plus Pydantic models for its transactions table. No cloud anything.
evals.expected_output: Profiles via usql DSN (information_schema + samples), generates one model per table with db types and constraints, generates a table-scoped instance (4-6 probes), count probe returns the true row count, coverage 100%.

evals.prompt: Our platform exports events as events.jsonl — one JSON object per line (timestamp, user_id, event_type, details with nested fields). Make this queryable in plain English through neuralOS with a strict model of the shape.
evals.expected_output: Profiler content-routes .jsonl to JSON-lines profiling with flattened dot-paths (incl. nested 'details.*'); gen_pydantic emits one model with aliases for any source keys that differ from Python identifiers; generated menu has peek/count_records/summary (+ by-column for low-cardinality fields); Phase 4 shows high parse coverage over the real records and one truth check against a direct file count.

evals.prompt: Fetch https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users, profile it, and build me a neuralOS instance over that data with a strict model.
evals.expected_output: The URL is fetched (4 MB cap, User-Agent set), content-sniffed as JSON (the extensionless body must route via sniffing, not fail as unrecognized), the nested user shape flattened (address.*, company.*) into a strict model with aliases, an instance generated with peek/count/summary probes, and verification run. If the fetch is unreachable, say so honestly instead of profiling garbage.

evals.prompt: Here's q3_ledger.xlsx with one sheet of transactions. Turn it into a neuralOS instance I can ask questions about in plain English.
evals.expected_output: XLSX profiling via openpyxl (values-only, first sheet, empty cells to null), dumped to a sniffed CSV bridge path; model generated from the header row; instance with peek/count_records/summary; Phase-4 coverage measured on real rows. If openpyxl is missing the profiler must say so in one clear line (pip install openpyxl), not crash.

evals.prompt: Build a neuralOS instance over data.db (a SQLite file on this machine) — I want plain-English queries and a strict model, no cloud anything.
evals.expected_output: SQLite profiling goes through the stdlib sqlite3 module (no usql needed): PRAGMA table_info for columns, sample rows, exact COUNT(*); a table-scoped instance generated with count/recent/summary probes; the count probe returns the true row count and Phase-4 coverage is measured live (target 100% on a clean table).
